summary: Small planned mixed-use block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan with a flat 90 ft height limit, located within PG&E's switchyard sub-area (whose redevelopment depends on PG&E's long-range facilities planning); program not confirmed beyond the D4D's generic use table, and no design review approval or construction start found.

milestones.text: Completion expected: Block 14 is in Phase 2 of the October 2020 re-phased program; SocketSite's block-by-block schedule for that program shows vertical development on Block 14 from 2029 to 2030, contingent on relocation of PG&E's switchyard
milestones.basis_note: Phase 2 in the October 7, 2020 Phase 1 and Phasing Plan Amendment approval (Figure 22 'Revised Phasing Plan'); SocketSite's (Oct 9, 2020) 'Re-Phase Program, Detailed Construction Schedule' table gives Block 14 vertical development 2029-2030. A 2020 forecast, not a commitment, and soft: the block lies in the PG&E Sub-area, whose built-out SF Planning says depends on relocation of the switchyard.

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement covering the adopted Design for Development, whose Land Use Table (Table 3.1.1) lists Block 14; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date

facts.value: Residential, Institutional, Retail and Non-Retail Sales/Services uses permitted; Laboratory and Life Science uses Not Permitted (D4D final Table 3.1.1)
flat 90 ft max per the D4D's Figure 6.2.3

Not listed among the six Phase 1 blocks (2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15) named in the 2024 annual compliance report, which does not mention Block 14 at all; the October 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval places it in Phase 2

Lies within the PG&E Sub-area, PG&E's roughly 4.8-acre switchyard parcel at 22nd and Illinois Streets (in the D4D's no-PG&E-Sub-area scenario, Blocks 13 and 14 are replaced by a single 'PG&E Sub-area'); the D4D says portions of the PG&E Sub-area 'may or may not ultimately be redeveloped'

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 14; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.
No source found for a specific intended use of Block 14 beyond the D4D's generic permitted-uses table; it is the smallest block on the site per the D4D's own Land Use Plan figure.

No block-specific schedule found beyond the 2020 forecast in SocketSite's table (Block 14 vertical development 2029-2030, Phase 2), which depends on PG&E relocating its switchyard; no PG&E relocation date was found.
